text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Mubarak in talks with Arafat and Kabariti on ways to get the peace process moving. Arafat says he gave Mubarak details on the negotiations and says that Isral has given Palestinians "racist" document on division of Hebron. Kabariti says he gave Mubarak message from King Hussein and denies there are plans for summit between Egypt, Jordan, Israel and the Palestinians in Amman.
- Arafat and Kabariti hold talks in Cairo.
- Paris Club drops last tranche of Egypt's debts to crown Mubarak's efforts at economic reform.
- Cabinet denies meningitis rumours but says vaccines are available as precaution.
- Four militants killed in shoot-out with police in Minya, two of them took part in shooting outside Europa hotel in which Greek tourists were killed.

- Kabariti says after meeting Mubarak that Jordan's position on peace is identical to Egypt's stance; says that he hopes American mediation can solve differences in current negotiations. Arafat presents "dangerous document that reveals Israel's intentions and blows up the agreements with Palestinians".
- Egyptian officials deny there is an Egyptian-French initiative to save peace process.
- After six months of searching and chasing, police catch terrorists who took part in Europa hotel attack and the killing of the lieutenant-general and his brother.
- Ganzouri receives word that Paris Club will drop $4.2 billion of Egypt's debts.
- Schools back to normal in Maadi.
- Mubarak met Arafat and Kabariti. Unified Egyptian and Jordanian position to boost Palestinian position.
